newsitem.title: FRANCE: Union says Mobil French refinery hit by go-slow.
newsitem.headline: Union says Mobil French refinery hit by go-slow.

text.p: A French union said on Thursday Mobil's 70,000 barrels per day (bpd) Gravenchon refinery in northern France was running at a slow pace in a new protest over jobs and working conditions.
There was no immediate confirmation from Mobil.
Disruption began on Wednesday evening and would last until Friday at 1300 GMT, the CFDT union, France's largest, said.
It said the refinery was running at the "minimum techhnical level," a device used to disrupt several refineries without halting them during widespread oil industry protests on Tuesday.
It also said unspecified action was planned at Esso's 150,000 bpd Port Jerome refinery near Gravenchon.

Unions said during a strike which slowed production at half France's refineries on Tuersday that further action was planned between Wednesday and Friday at Mobil's single French plant and between Thursday and saturday at two French Esso refineries.
The disruption is over oil industry plans to cut some 1,500 refinery jobs over the next year to deal with overcapacity.
